steps.description: @assertion the startup "Welcome to VS Code" sign-in overlay is visible and its Close button is available.
Click the Close button on the startup Welcome sign-in overlay.
@assertion the startup sign-in overlay is no longer visible and the VS Code workbench is ready.
Press the F1 key to open the Command Palette in Visual Studio Code.
@assertion the Visual Studio Code Command Palette is visible with a > character in its input box and is ready to accept a command search.

parameters.text: Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit: Focus on Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit View

steps.description: Type the resolved command title into the active Command Palette.

@assertion the Command Palette input box reads >Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit: Focus on Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit View and the highlighted command listed under it is titled Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit: Focus on Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit View.
Press Enter to execute the selected Command Palette command.
@assertion the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit view is open in the side bar and an editor tab labeled Welcome showing the Build a Declarative Agent walkthrough is open in the editor area.
@assertion the editor tab labeled Welcome showing the Build a Declarative Agent walkthrough is the active editor tab in the Visual Studio Code editor area.
Press Ctrl+W to close the Welcome editor tab.
@assertion no editor tab is open in the Visual Studio Code editor area.
Press the F1 key to open the Command Palette in Visual Studio Code.
@assertion the Visual Studio Code Command Palette is visible with a > character in its input box and is ready to accept a command search.
Type the resolved command title into the active Command Palette.
@assertion the Command Palette input box reads >Microsoft 365 Agents: Create New Agent/App and the highlighted command listed under it is titled Microsoft 365 Agents: Create New Agent/App.
Press Enter to execute the selected Command Palette command.
@assertion the active prompt titled New Project is visible.
@assertion the prompt titled New Project has finished loading and lists at least one selectable option.
Type the resolved option label Teams Agents and Apps into the active single-select prompt.
@assertion the option Teams Agents and Apps is visible and selectable in the filtered single-select prompt.
Press Enter to confirm the filtered single-select option.
@assertion the active prompt titled Teams Agent or App Using Microsoft Teams SDK is visible.
@assertion the prompt titled Teams Agent or App Using Microsoft Teams SDK has finished loading and lists at least one selectable option.
Type the resolved option label Other Teams Capabilities into the active single-select prompt.
@assertion the option Other Teams Capabilities is visible and selectable in the filtered single-select prompt.
Press Enter to confirm the filtered single-select option.
@assertion the active prompt titled Teams Capability is visible.
@assertion the prompt titled Teams Capability has finished loading and lists at least one selectable option.
Type the resolved option label Tab into the active single-select prompt.
@assertion the option Tab is visible and selectable in the filtered single-select prompt.
Press Enter to confirm the filtered single-select option.
@assertion the active prompt titled Workspace Folder is visible and the option Default folder is focused.
Press Enter to confirm the Default folder option.
@assertion the active prompt titled Application Name is visible.
Type the authored value into the active text prompt.
Press Enter to submit the accepted text input.
@assertion the Preview README.md editor tab is open in Visual Studio Code.

Language: bash

```bash
set -euo pipefail
PROJECT_DIR="/home/vscode/AgentsToolkitProjects/${{var:app_name}}" ASSERTIONS_B64="W3sicGF0aCI6Im0zNjVhZ2VudHMueW1sIiwiZXhpc3RzIjp0cnVlLCJjb250YWlucyI6WyJ2ZXJzaW9uOiB2MS4xMSIsInByb3Zpc2lvbjoiLCJkZXBsb3k6IiwiYXp1cmVBcHBTZXJ2aWNlL3ppcERlcGxveSJdLCJub3RDb250YWlucyI6W119XQ==" python3 - <<'PY'
import base64
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

project = Path(os.environ["PROJECT_DIR"]).resolve()
assertions = json.loads(base64.b64decode(os.environ["ASSERTIONS_B64"]).decode("utf-8"))
for assertion in assertions:
    target = (project / assertion["path"]).resolve()
    try:
        target.relative_to(project)
    except ValueError as error:
        raise AssertionError("File assertion escaped the project directory") from error
    exists = target.is_file()
    if exists != assertion["exists"]:
        raise AssertionError(f"Unexpected file existence for {assertion['path']}")
    if not exists:
        continue
    content = target.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    for expected in assertion.get("contains", []):
        expected = expected.replace("__VSCUSE_APP_NAME__", project.name)
        if expected not in content:
            raise AssertionError(f"Expected content is absent from {assertion['path']}")
    for unexpected in assertion.get("notContains", []):
        unexpected = unexpected.replace("__VSCUSE_APP_NAME__", project.name)
        if unexpected in content:
            raise AssertionError(f"Unexpected content is present in {assertion['path']}")
PY
```

steps.description: @code verify the authored workspace file existence and content assertions without logging file contents.
Press the F1 key to open the Command Palette in Visual Studio Code.
@assertion the Visual Studio Code Command Palette is visible with a > character in its input box and is ready to accept a command search.
Type the resolved command title into the active Command Palette.
@assertion the Command Palette input box reads >View: Show Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit and the highlighted command listed under it is titled View: Show Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.
Press Enter to execute the selected Command Palette command.
@assertion the ACCOUNTS section of the side bar lists an entry whose label begins with Sign in to Microsoft.
Click the entry whose label begins with "Sign in to Microsoft" in the ACCOUNTS section of the side bar.
Click the "Sign in" button within the Microsoft 365 developer sandbox modal.
Click on the "Email or phone" input field in the Microsoft Sign-in form on the login.microsoftonline.com webpage to focus the cursor for credential entry.
Enter the resolved Microsoft 365 account name into the email or username input field on the Microsoft Sign in page.
Click the blue "Next" button on the Microsoft sign-in page, confirming the entered email address for login.
Type the resolved Microsoft 365 account password into the Password field on the Microsoft login page.
Press Enter to submit the Microsoft 365 login form from the password entry screen.
Click the "Close" button (red cross icon) in the browser tab bar to close the "M365 Account - Sign In" page.
@assertion the "ACCOUNTS" section lists an entry whose label is ${{env:M365_ACCOUNT_NAME}} or that name cut short by the side bar with a trailing ellipsis.
Press the F1 key to open the Command Palette in Visual Studio Code.
@assertion the Visual Studio Code Command Palette is visible with a > character in its input box and is ready to accept a command search.
Type the resolved command title into the active Command Palette.
@assertion the Command Palette input box reads >Debug: Select and Start Debugging and the highlighted command listed under it is titled Debug: Select and Start Debugging.
Press Enter to execute the selected Command Palette command.
Type the resolved option label into the active option picker.
@assertion the option Debug in Teams (Chrome) is visible and selectable in the filtered option picker.
Press Enter to confirm the filtered option.
@assertion the Microsoft sign-in page in Chrome names ${{env:M365_ACCOUNT_NAME}} and asks for that account's password.
Click the password input on the Microsoft sign-in page to move focus out of the browser address bar.
Enter the registered Microsoft 365 password in the focused password input of the browser sign-in form.
Press Enter to submit the Microsoft 365 password.
@assertion the Microsoft Stay signed in question is visible with Yes focused.
Press Enter to confirm staying signed in.
@assertion the Microsoft Teams app details page for an app whose name starts with ${{var:app_name}} is visible.
@assertion Microsoft Teams is the displayed page in Google Chrome and the Chrome tab bar shows its new-tab button to the right of the open tabs.
Click the new-tab (+) button in the Google Chrome tab bar.
@assertion a new empty Google Chrome tab is displayed with its address bar ready for typing.
Type the local tab page address https://localhost:3978/tabs/home into the Google Chrome address bar.
Press Enter to navigate to the typed local tab page address.
@assertion the Google Chrome certificate warning page for localhost is displayed with the button that expands its details.
Click the "Advanced" button on the Google Chrome certificate warning page for localhost.
@assertion the expanded Google Chrome certificate warning shows the link that continues to localhost anyway.
Click the "Proceed to localhost (unsafe)" link on the expanded Google Chrome certificate warning page.
@assertion the page served from https://localhost:3978 is displayed instead of the certificate warning, and the Microsoft Teams tab is still open in the Google Chrome tab bar.
Click the Microsoft Teams tab in the Google Chrome tab bar to return to it.
@assertion Microsoft Teams is again the displayed page in Google Chrome.
@assertion the app details popup is visible with its primary action button below the app name.
Click the visible blue "Add" or "Open" button in the Microsoft Teams app details dialog.
@assertion the dialog that the app details popup opened is visible with its Open button.
Click the blue "Open" button in the "Added successfully!" or "Let's go" dialog for the app in Microsoft Teams.
@assertion the Microsoft Teams tab page for an app whose name starts with ${{var:app_name}} is open.
@assertion Google Chrome is displaying a teams.cloud.microsoft permission prompt that asks to access other apps and services on this device and its Allow button is available.
Click Allow in the teams.cloud.microsoft permission prompt that asks to access other apps and services on this device.

@assertion the teams.cloud.microsoft permission prompt asking to access other apps and services on this device is no longer visible and the Microsoft Teams tab page remains displayed in Google Chrome.
@assertion the page the current target opened contains "Your app is running in TeamsModern".
